Phases run in order; P0 (ADOPT + STYLE DISCOVERY) waits for the owner by design and needs task.mjs signoff and task.mjs archsignoff before its gate passes. Later phases are added by the planner at the end of P0 (task.mjs phase-add) from the game's real state.

phases.name: Foundation: drive and walk the real pilot centre
phases.goal: Pillar 3 (the city opens up) and the base under all three pillars. The pilot centre (about 20 km2: Connaught Place with Jantar Mantar, India Gate, ITO with Pragati Maidan, Chandni Chowk with Red Fort, Paharganj with the station, GB Road and everything between) is baked from real map data through the repair layer and the lane-level road model, streams in Godot, and can be driven and walked with the signed vehicle and on-foot numbers. Solid before rich: no overlaps, no floating roads, collisions match what is drawn, north is up. The map inspector comes first so Anmol can review issues during the pilot.
exit: npm run bake -- pilot builds the pilot centre twice with identical tile hashes, and the map health report gate counts (open ports, floating ends, unjoined ends, overlapping road faces, broken lane continuity, tapers out of limits) are 0 or each one is explained

the base tests the owner asked for pass in the real city: landmark pins within tolerance and on the right side of the map, collider against drawn surface within 0.05 m, north up on the map and -Z in the world, no mirrored node
streaming at 200 km/h has no frame over 33 ms and the city path perf scenarios are inside the signed budgets
the car reaches 140 km/h and the car, auto, scooter and on-foot numbers are inside the GAME.md ranges, measured by feel probe scenarios

the map inspector shows issues and lanes, and an override written from it is used by the next bake
FD0 plays in the real pilot centre and a Mac test build runs it
verify --all is green
playtest: Read this first: buildings are plain box placeholders, there is no traffic, no people and no missions beyond FD0. Judge the ground, roads, movement and feel, not the looks of the buildings. Start with npm run play.
Frame rate: watch the FPS counter top left while you drive and walk. Does it stay smooth in the CP circle, on the radials and on the ITO flyover? Note where it dips.
Drive the auto around the CP circle and out along the radials. Does the car feel heavy enough, turn well and stop well? Is the camera easy to read at speed?
Drive up and over the ITO flyover and back under it. Do the ramps join the road, and do the lanes under and over line up without gaps?
Ground fit: look for roads floating above the ground or sunk into it, at junctions, kerbs and flyover ramps. Tell me the place if you see one.
Roads joining: at the big junctions, do roads meet cleanly with no overlaps, holes or flickering patches? Are railings only where they should be?
Get out of the auto and get back in. Does it feel quick and clear, and does the camera switch well in both directions?
Walk, jog and sprint, then jump and vault low walls. Do the speeds feel right, and does the camera stay sensible near walls?
Kerbs and stairs: walk up and down kerbs and steps. Do you step smoothly or get stuck or pop upward?
Walk into the Chandni Chowk gali. Is it too narrow or too tight, and does the camera cope? Does it feel like a lane in Old Delhi?
Landmarks: go to India Gate and the Red Fort. Are they in the right place and about the right size, even as placeholders?
Anything floating, sunk, flickering or stuck anywhere else: write down where, so I can add a fix task.

tasks.title: Harness baseline on the scaffold: coordinate contract, drive scenarios, FD0
tasks.desc: The scaffold already has window.__game (src/debug/hooks.ts) and verify --quick was green on 2026-11-10. Lock the baseline and the coordinate rule (owner inbox: correct coordinates from day 1 with tests). (1) Check the hook contract against docs/GAME_HOOKS.md and fix any gap; without ?debug=1 window.__game.debug must not exist (add a unit test or a scenario that opens the page without debug=1). (2) Add src/geo/projection.ts: lat/lon to world metres and back around one named Delhi origin constant (India Gate, 28.612894 N, 77.229446 E), east +X, north -Z, up +Y, accurate to under 0.5 m within 25 km of the origin (local transverse Mercator or ENU; write the choice to decisions.md as provisional until the architecture sign-off). No mirroring, no axis flips. (3) Unit tests: the origin maps to (0,0); Connaught Place central park (28.6315, 77.2167) lands at x -1246 +/- 25, z -2071 +/- 25 (north-west of the origin); Red Fort (28.6562, 77.2410) lands at x +1129 +/- 25, z -4821 +/- 25 (north-north-east); round trip error under 0.01 m; a point due north has x 0 and negative z. (4) Scenarios (input only, wait in sim time): drive_north (throttle 3 s from heading 0: z falls by over 10 m, abs x under 0.5 m), drive_turn_right (throttle plus steer right: heading grows and x becomes positive), coords_north_marker (camera at the origin looking north shows the red north post in the centre third of the shot; the builder reads the shot). (5) Play script harness/verify/milestones/FD0.js per milestones.json FD0 (real inputs only). (6) quick.json: core = boot_title, hooks_contract, perf_baseline, drive_north; areas mapped to src/car.ts, src/geo/, src/debug/. Notes: this is tooling and tests, no look change.
accept: npm run typecheck and npm test pass; the projection tests named above exist and pass (CP and Red Fort within 25 m of the given x and z, round trip under 0.01 m)

node harness/bin/verify.mjs --only hooks_contract,boot_title,drive_north,drive_turn_right,coords_north_marker passes with no console errors, and the builder read coords_north_marker.png (red post centred, ahead)
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --milestone FD0 passes
a check proves window.__game.debug is undefined when the page opens without ?debug=1
node harness/bin/verify.mjs --quick passes and node harness/bin/verify.mjs --all passes (or each failure is listed as a known bug task)
decisions.md has the provisional projection entry; TECH.md 'Coordinates' names src/geo/projection.ts and its tests
tasks.summary: Transverse Mercator projection around India Gate, no flips; CP and Red Fort land within 25 m; drive_north, drive_turn_right, coords_north_marker, hooks_no_debug scenarios and FD0 pass; quick 7/7. verify --all deferred to the P0 gate (low usage mode).

tasks.title: Salvage and quality audit of the old game (read only)
tasks.desc: Owner inbox part 1: a SALVAGE AUDIT of /Users/apple/Desktop/code/delhi-drive, read only (never edit, build, install, run npm or write there). Write harness/design/SALVAGE_AUDIT.md: one table row per item with verdict KEEP (copy after a check), REWRITE (keep the idea, new code), DROP, with evidence (file:line, numbers) and the reason. Cover: data sources and their licences (OSM PBF, Copernicus GLO-30 and why a surface model makes roads float or sink), bake knowledge in backend/worldBuilder/buildRegion.js (projection, tiling at zoom 16, 500 m tiles, binary format, what it did right and wrong), car tuning numbers and the handling model, the 580 frontend tests (read for intent: which checks are worth rewriting as tests here), assets in art-src and frontend/public (quality, licence, Delhi relevance: paan stains, political posters, textures), the lessons in README, TECHNICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md, docs/, TODO.md and CLAUDE.md, and the root cause of each base-layer failure: the mirror axis (worldGroup.scale.x = -1 and negated physics px), overlapping road meshes, misplaced railings, junctions that do not join, terrain and road misfit, tileManager.js at 2346 lines, the leftover cannon-es layer, the 11 GB JSON tiles. End with 'What Dilli Darshan must do differently' (one line each, feeds ARCH_OPTIONS). Then write harness/design/QUALITY_AUDIT.md from harness/design/templates/QUALITY_AUDIT.template.md, 'why it felt thin', scored against a polish and richness bar for a Delhi driving game (visuals, feel: handling, speed sense, camera, FOV, shake; audio: engine, horns, ambience; VFX: dust, smoke, skid marks, heat haze; traffic and life; UI and HUD; performance), every finding with evidence from the old game and a fix size, plus 'What to protect' (the good parts). Evidence for shots: if the already built frontend/dist can be served read only by a static server started from THIS repo (for example the harness static server pointed at that folder) without writing into the old repo, take a few shots and read them; if it needs its backend or fails, rely on code, docs and art files and say so. The owner reads both docs before the style interview, so put a 10 line summary at the top of each.

tasks.title: Game design options draft (GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY)
tasks.desc: Mode GAME_DESIGN_DISCOVERY (owner direction 2026-11-10, inbox mmwap8jxg: a car driving around Delhi is a tech demo, not a game). Write harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md with comparison tables and small text sketches (loop diagrams, a sample mission beat sheet, a HUD sketch) covering his 7 points: 1. fantasy options (new auto driver, delivery rider, cabbie who knows every gali, tourist guide, street racer, a mix), one sentence each plus why it fits Delhi; 2. the core loop at 30 s, 5 min and 1 h per fantasy, and the tension sources (traffic, time, money, rivals, police, weather, fares); 3. a big list (40 or more) of Delhi missions and activities (fares, deliveries, races, chases, festivals, wedding baraat routes, monsoon floods, rush hour, night runs, sightseeing tours past real landmarks, side jobs, collectibles) ranked by fun, uniqueness, build effort and map reuse; 4. progression and reasons to return (money, vehicle unlocks and upgrades, reputation by area, unlocking parts of the city, daily and weekly jobs, story or characters, personal bests and leaderboards, photo spots), each marked healthy or chore with the reason; 5. game feel (speed sense, near misses, horn culture, weaving through traffic, drifts, landmarks as rewards) and 3 candidate sets of feel pillars; 6. honest scope: the smallest first playable loop that is already fun in the pilot area (Connaught Place, ITO and Pragati Maidan, Chandni Chowk, one metro line), then what grows from it, each option with fun, cost, risk and needs from the map, AI traffic and art; 7. references (known open world and driving games): what fits, what to avoid; inspiration, never copy. Use the old game's modes (dash, taxi, delivery, free, police, see SALVAGE_AUDIT.md) as evidence of what was tried. End with a recommendation and at most 6 short, clear questions for round 1, each with options. Never invent the owner's answers.

tasks.title: Interview sitting 1: style, place and game design round 1

tasks.title: Delhi street stand-in scene and perf baseline (Godot)

In the Godot project add a procedural stand-in Delhi street built by a GDScript builder (for example game/scenes/standin/), reusable by style tests and benches, loaded with debug.load('street') or --scene=street; the default boot is unchanged. From CITY_BRIEF.md: about 300 m of a 6 lane arterial with a median and kerbs, a service lane, one signal junction, a stub flyover ramp (a simple stand-in, not the lane model), footpaths, 40 to 80 box buildings with shopfront bands and sign boards, trees, street lights, a bus stop, 15 to 25 static vehicles (car, auto-rickshaw, bus stand-ins), 20 to 40 people stand-ins (capsules or simple mannequins), and one third-person character stand-in for on-foot views. Landmarks and areas, loaded with 'landmarks' and 'areas' (or placed along the street): one stand-in per tier (hero: an India Gate like arch from a small parts kit; signature: a domed tomb on a plinth or a CP style colonnade block; marker: an extruded footprint with an area material), each with its surroundings (lawn, wall, gate, parking), and two contrasting area kit blocks of about 100 m each (old city bazaar strip: tight shop houses, wires, signs, vendors; Lutyens bungalow road: walls, trees, low white bungalows). Then write harness/look_proof/poses.json with 9 views (car close-up, street at driving eye height, junction, flyover ramp, HUD over play, busiest view from 40 m up, landmark tiers from the road at player height, the two area blocks from 30 m up, on foot at 1.7 m eye height in the bazaar strip; sim held, same moment every run), run node harness/bin/lookproof.mjs --set baseline --perf, read the shots, and write draft budgets in harness/verify/perf_budgets.json (status stays draft) from the measured numbers with headroom, with the target filled in (machine, Godot version, renderer, GPU, resolution, load). tasks.title: Architecture options draft for Godot and the composite map (with map repair, lane model and map inspector)
tasks.desc: Mode ARCH_DISCOVERY, now for Godot 4.7 on desktop (Mac and Windows; a web demo maybe later) and the composite map. Write harness/design/ARCH_OPTIONS.md from templates/ARCH_OPTIONS.template.md, using SALVAGE_AUDIT.md 'What Dilli Darshan must do differently', the Godot baseline perf numbers (P0-009), the style candidates, the owner's answers from sittings 1 and 2 (three characters, guns and fights, on foot anywhere, the composite map districts and layout), and the leading game design options. Decisions, 2 to 4 options each, every number marked estimate or measured: renderer (Forward+ vs Mobile; lighting at city scale: baked lightmaps vs SDFGI vs VoxelGI vs no GI with tuned ambient); physics (Jolt vs Godot Physics; VehicleBody3D vs a custom raycast vehicle; CharacterBody3D for on foot; collider shapes per tile: concave trimesh vs HeightMapShape3D plus road meshes); language (GDScript vs C#, which blocks the web export and needs the .NET build and a dotnet SDK, vs GDExtension in C++ or Rust for heavy runtime code); the offline bake pipeline outside Godot (Node reusing tools/geo/projection.ts, vs Python) and what Godot reads (custom binary tiles parsed in GDScript or GDExtension, Godot resources written by a headless Godot import step, or glTF per tile); coordinates (district frames: a transverse Mercator origin per district plus a translation offset, MAP_REPAIR.md 'District frames and stitching'; float precision at the planned map size: 32-bit floats, a floating origin, or a double precision build); the composite map (district selection file, clip and offset, stitching, connector authoring format and tools, filler between districts, the layout options from DELHI_WORLD.md section 0 with the owner's answers); tile streaming and memory (ResourceLoader threaded loads or WorkerThreadPool, tile size, unload, memory per tile); instancing and LOD (MultiMesh, visibility ranges and HLOD, impostors, occlusion culling); textures (VRAM compression on Mac and Windows, atlases); navigation (navmesh baked per tile offline vs at load; agents for pedestrians, police and traffic); animation and crowds (AnimationTree with skinned characters vs vertex animation in MultiMesh for far crowds, LOD); combat runtime (hitscan, projectiles, ragdolls); traffic AI on the lane model; the map repair layer (refine MAP_REPAIR.md: sources with licence, attribution and quality checks, the pipeline with district selection and stitching, rule engine, auto-repair log, per-tile overrides, elevation solver, verification, pilot districts); the lane-level road model; the road graph to junction mesh builder; terrain that conforms to roads; the map inspector (a web page reading baked data vs a Godot tool scene or editor plugin: fly-to, proposed fixes as 3D preview lines with confidence and reasoning, writes per-tile overrides and the inbox, lane widths and splits, area and landmark views); the verify harness on Godot (the debug server and driver from P0-025 to P0-027: keep or change); export and packaging (Mac signing and notarising, Windows build); budgets per system. Delhi world layers (DELHI_WORLD.md): decision rows for (a) the landmark registry pipeline (sources and matching, storage, tier scoring, placement inside the district frame, hero model limits and LOD, stand-in parts kit), (b) the area profile pipeline (area division, profile storage, generator at bake time vs in the game, kits and atlases, edge blending, determinism, filler between districts), (c) the inspector area and landmark views. (2) Sim clock C1: one engine physics frame is one sim tick; the time scale sets Engine.time_scale and Engine.physics_ticks_per_second together so the step stays 1/60 s; the hold stops SimClock and calls PhysicsServer3D.set_active(false) (the engine has no manual space step). tasks.title: Godot debug server: the hook contract inside the game
tasks.desc: Implement docs/GAME_HOOKS.md in the Godot game so the harness can drive it. (1) An autoload in game/debug/ that exists only when the game is started with the user arg --debug (after the -- separator). It listens on 127.0.0.1 (port from --debug-port, default from kit.config.json godot.debugPort) over WebSocket or TCP with JSON messages, one request id per call. (2) Methods: every required hook (state, clock, frames, input, perf, load, teleport, setCamera, timeScale, hold, events, hud) plus shot(path) (viewport image saved as PNG after the frame is drawn), quit, and quality if cheap. Snapshot push: after every drawn frame the server sends a small snapshot (state, clock, hold, the newest events) so the harness can answer the synchronous hooks (state, clock, hold, events) from the latest snapshot; frames, perf, load and shot are request and response. (3) Sim clock with time scale and the sim hold, read by every game system that steps (the car now; later physics, AI and missions), with a fixed physics tick. (4) perf(ms): cpuMs and gpuMs p50, p95 and max per frame (RenderingServer viewport measured CPU and GPU render times plus process time), p95FrameMs, avgFps, drawCalls and triangles (RenderingServer total draw calls and primitives in frame), gpuMB (video memory used). (5) CLI user args replace the page params: --debug, --verify (hides every debug overlay), --quality=<preset>, --style=<name>, --scene=<id>, --arch=<name>, --lockstep, --mute, --resolution handled by Godot itself. (6) Without --debug: no port opens, the debug node does not exist, the game plays the same. (7) Errors: expected situations never call push_error; unexpected ones are also sent as an 'error' event. (8) docs/GAME_HOOKS.md: add a 'Godot transport' section (args, message format, snapshot vs request, shot) and mark the browser params as the web demo path (later). Add game/debug/ to shared_paths.json.

tasks.desc: Seed from the game plan (owner: decisions.md "Cutscenes and story telling"; signed design: TECH.md "Story runtime (CS2, DG1, LIP2 then LIP1, FC2, SB1, SK1)"). tasks.title: Dialogue line player, Hinglish and English subtitles, and the jaw
tasks.desc: Seed from the game plan (TECH.md "Story runtime": DG1, SB1, LIP2; STORY_OUTLINE.md section 5 for the talk rules). game/story/dialogue_player.gd and subtitles.gd, with game/characters/face.gd for the jaw. Pillar: three lives, one city (most of the story is told in play: drive talk, phone, inner voice).

tasks.title: Road width continuity: no sudden thick to thin, lanes change only with a proper merge
tasks.desc: Anmol 2026-11-13 with a screenshot of Kartavya Path and the road crossing it near India Gate (harness/reports/map/anmol_2026-11-13_kartavya_width_jumps.png): the north-south road is thick on one side of the crossing and thin on the other, and the roads round the small triangles and the garden go thick then suddenly thin. That is not how such roads are built: a 3 or 4 lane road does not become 2 lanes without a proper merge. Rules for the lane model: (1) a road keeps one cross section along a corridor (same name or same class through a junction, collinear within about 20 degrees) unless there is real evidence for a change (a lane tag that agrees with photos, a junction with turn lanes, a slip road leaving); OSM segments with a missing or odd lanes tag take the corridor's width, not a class default; (2) where the width does change, it changes with a taper of the proper length for the speed (lane drop or add, about 1:20 to 1:30), never a step; (3) slip roads and the roads round triangle islands and garden edges get a width that fits their role (one or two lanes) and join the main road through gores and tapers; (4) a new check counts width steps (a change of more than 1 m within 5 m along a corridor) and fails the bake on any that is not inside a taper. Use real-life references (photos, satellite) for the hero stretches here: Kartavya Path, the road crossing it near the canals, the India Gate hexagon approaches. Acceptance: (a) width steps over the whole pilot 0, each former step listed with what fixed it; (b) before and after map renders of this exact site and of two other sites under harness/reports/map/; (c) whole bake green with gates explained, stream and city route fixtures regenerated, test block rebaked; (d) lane model unit tests for corridor width carry-over and tapers; (e) typecheck, npm test and verify --quick green.

tasks.title: On-foot movement that feels like a real game, not cartoonish
tasks.desc: Anmol 2026-11-14: running feels cartoonish, not like a real game. Cause (P1-023): the free CC0 clips are slower than the game's speeds, so walk plays at 1.86x and sprint at 1.95x (quick, bouncy cadence); no starts, stops or turn animations; no lean, no foot placement; the body snaps between states. Target: grounded, weighty, filmi but never cheap (STYLE_BIBLE 'snappy and weighty', reference feel of GTA V and Watch Dogs 2 third person). Build: (1) locomotion clips whose stride matches the game speeds so playback stays within 0.9 to 1.15x (other CC0 sets, retargeted and stride-measured; or adjust walk, jog and sprint speeds within GAME.md ranges to the clips' natural cadence, with a decision line); (2) a speed and direction blend space instead of hard state switches, with start, stop and plant-and-turn clips; (3) acceleration and deceleration curves on the character so speed does not jump; (4) lean into turns and slight forward lean at sprint, head look toward the camera direction; (5) foot IK on kerbs, stairs and slopes; (6) a subtle camera follow lag and sprint shake that never jitters. Never ask Anmol for animation files.
accept: Playback rate of walk, jog and sprint between 0.9 and 1.15 (printed)
Foot slide under 5 percent at walk, jog and sprint
Start, stop and 180 degree turn each blend without a pop (frame-to-frame bone change under a set limit, test)
Feet on kerbs and stairs within 3 cm of the surface (IK test)
A verifier reads a frame strip of a run, start, stop and turn at the play camera and judges it grounded, not bouncy or cartoonish
Cost per character still 0.05 ms or less; typecheck, npm test and verify --quick green
tasks.summary: Locomotion rebuilt for feel: built walk, jog and sprint clips play at 0.9996x (cadence 130, 166, 204 steps a minute), speed and direction blend with start, stop and plant-and-turn, acceleration curves, lean, head look, two-bone leg IK (p95 0.4 to 1.0 cm on kerbs and stairs), calm camera follow; model no longer floats 8 cm. Verifier PASS: slide 1.0 to 1.5%, no pops, quick 12/12, foot_cost ok alone; reads as a real runner, GTA-like, not cartoonish. Polish on the 180 turn pose in P14-005.

tasks.title: Who may use each road: car-free streets, two-wheeler galis, footways, bollards and gates
tasks.desc: Anmol 2026-11-14: some roads are roads but cars cannot go. Today the road graph treats every highway class as drivable and drops footways and pedestrian streets entirely (tools/bake/graph/features.ts keeps only foot bridges); OSM access tags are not read. Build an access model per edge and lane: allowed modes (car, auto, two-wheeler, cycle and rickshaw, pedestrian, emergency and police) from OSM access, motor_vehicle, motorcar, vehicle and highway tags, barriers (bollards, gates, kerbs, lift gates) and Delhi rules from references: Chandni Chowk main road car-free in the day (only pedestrians, rickshaws and emergency), old city galis for two-wheelers and walkers only, Kartavya Path promenade and lawn paths pedestrian, government and Lutyens gates, metro and station forecourts. Build pedestrian streets, footways and plazas as walkable surfaces in the mesh (not dropped), with bollards and gate props where the access changes. Write the modes into the lane graph and tiles so traffic AI, the route line (GPS) and missions respect them. Player driving into a car-free street: bollards or barriers stop cars where they exist in reality; elsewhere it is allowed but a violation (later: police and wanted level reaction). Real-life references: photos for Chandni Chowk's bollards and the gali entries.
accept: Access modes on every edge and lane, counts per mode in health.json; Chandni Chowk main road car-free, galis two-wheeler and foot only, footways and pedestrian streets present as walkable surfaces
Bollards and gates placed where access changes, with colliders that stop a car (scenario: a car is stopped at the Chandni Chowk bollards, a scooter passes into a gali)
Lane graph and route data exclude car edges where cars are not allowed (test)

Whole bake green with gates explained; typecheck, npm test and verify --quick green

Include the India Gate and Kartavya Path car-free stretches: the paved promenade and roads inside the India Gate lawns and around the canopy, closed to cars and open to walkers (barriers at the hexagon); check against current photos and satellite, since closures changed after the Central Vista redevelopment. Also the Kartavya Path east of the hexagon that P1-046 noted as about 14 m of paving: it is a pedestrian promenade, not a car road.

Anmol 2026-11-14: 'it's not even OSM rules, we have to have common sense too for some areas.' OSM access tags are only one input; most car-free places are untagged. Add common-sense rules and a judge pass: (1) width: a way narrower than a car plus margins (under about 2.8 m) is not for cars; under about 1.6 m not for two-wheelers; (2) context: paths inside parks, lawns, monument grounds, campuses and housing compounds, ghats and river banks, market and bazaar lanes, temple, mosque and gurdwara precincts, metro and station forecourts, plazas, steps and ramps are foot-first; (3) surface and shape: unpaved, steps, dead-end stubs into compounds, gated entries are not through roads for cars; (4) a top-view judge pass with satellite and street photos (tools/inspector/judge.mjs) for anything unclear, deciding like a person who knows Delhi, each decision written as a patch with its reason; (5) Anmol's word or the inspector overrides everything.
